title: One More Broadside
author: OneMoreCrew
selftext:
Ahoy,

I've been quietly working on a game in the little spare time I have after work and family time and I'd love to share it with you all.

I'm a software engineer by trade but always wanted to try my hand at game development but honestly haven't had the time. The advent of AI has allowed me the opportunity to build something I genuinely enjoy playing that realistically I would never have made otherwise. 

Workflow has mostly involved iterative development with Claude - Opus 5.5 on high and some small usage of GPT (mostly just to try out astra when it came out).

Ive been dabbling with Godot and Unity for a while (both pre and post AI) but having seen the success some people were having with JS based games decided to give it a whirl with electron which also allowed me to target for mobile and pc. I also wanted to try out an asset tool called Kiln https://github.com/instruktlabs/kiln

Which turned out to be very useful for generating ships and objects having not had a huge amount of luck just generating assets with raw models and not fancying going the tripio etc route just from a cost perspective.

Sound effects was interesting using a mix of procedural stuff and free open source assets. I found that having Claude build a basic sound board where I could compare sound effects/volumes and the various levels of reverb/grit/echo etc was a godsend for getting something that sounded ok.

Music was a bit of a shot in the dark and I went with mureka.ai - started with a trial and ended up getting a year sub. Spent a decent amount of time tweaking lyrics and styles to get songs that worked for my eclectic taste. I found it to be decent but hit and miss with a somewhat limited range of voices and a habit of sneaking in repeated melodies (luckily this sort of ties most of the songs together thematically so I didn't mind it so much). My family are probably somewhat sick of the songs now having had them playing almost on loop in our living room for the last month or so!

As I have been targeting both mobile and pc I found that hosting a little server to download the latest apk on my phone for quick tests locally to be pretty handy - playtest, ping Claude with feedback over remote control, redownload APK, go again. 

Fairly early on I got Claude to build a series of test play throughs with various builds and a sort of maths stats run to ensure changes to builds didn't break the game balance or the actual game mechanics/navigation. I also enforced a fairly strict documentation regime that required all updates to be recorded in the appropriate documentation files - this reduced (I hope) mistakes by  the agents. 

I'm in the final stages of review with steam, Google play and apple app store. Luckily had a mix of family and friends with patience and different devices to test on - Googles 14 day closed testing with 12+ testers would have been quite a challenge otherwise I suspect for a solo dev! 

Anyway rambled on enough - happy to answer questions. If you like the look of the game I would be grateful for a wishlist - demo will be put as soon as the build is approved and I'm hoping Google and apple greenlight soon.

Olly
